S. aureus makes no endotoxin; its superantigen activates T cells directly by bridging MHC II and TCR Vβ
The staphylococcal toxin must first be processed and presented by MHC II, so the block acts too late
The shock comes from staphylococcal ADP-ribosylation of EF-2, which CD14 blockade cannot reverse

stem: A 3-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial sinus and lung infections. Serum IgM is elevated; IgG, IgA and IgE are very low. His B-cell count is normal. Genetic testing finds a mutation in an X-linked gene expressed on activated CD4+ T cells. Besides isotype switching, which B-cell process is most directly expected to be impaired?

options: V(D)J recombination of heavy-chain genes in bone-marrow pro-B cells
Affinity maturation of antibodies in germinal centers
Co-expression of membrane IgM and IgD on naive B cells by alternative splicing
Secretion of pentameric IgM by plasma cells
Signal transduction through Igα/Igβ after BCR cross-linking

Naive B cells make IgM and IgD by alternative splicing without T-cell help. [L060 p3]
IgM secretion is preserved; the elevated IgM is the hallmark of the syndrome. [L065 p9]
Igα/Igβ carry the BCR's own signal (the CD3 analog). The faculty separates this from the CD40/CD40L T-cell help signal that drives switching and affinity maturation. [L064 p2; 075 05:57-06:42]

stem: A 6-year-old girl with autosomal recessive AID deficiency received the full primary tetanus series in infancy and is not receiving immunoglobulin replacement. She now gets a booster. Compared with a healthy child, which serum response is expected over the next 1-2 weeks?
sourceRef: OST520 (064, 065) L - B Cells and Antibodies I and II - Taylor.pdf, file pp. 4-5, 9
options: A rapid, high-affinity IgG response, because memory B cells formed during the primary series
No antibody of any isotype, because B cells cannot be activated without AID
Normal IgG but absent IgA and IgE, because AID is needed only for mucosal and allergic isotypes
High-affinity IgM, because affinity maturation proceeds even though switching fails
An IgM-dominant response without a rise in high-affinity IgG

AID is required to switch to any downstream isotype, IgG included. Deficiency leaves IgM only. [L064 p4]
Affinity maturation also needs AID (cytosine to uracil, corrected to thymine). Without it, affinity maturation fails as well. [L064 p4]

AID deficiency is an autosomal recessive hyper-IgM form, so output is IgM only. AID's C-to-U deamination is needed both for switch-region breaks and for variable-region point mutations, so the IgM is also not affinity-matured. [L064 p4; L065 p9]

rationale:

stem: NK-cell Fc receptor (CD number) that triggers ADCC, and the killing mediators released
rationale:
Answer: CD16 (activating Fcγ receptor on NK cells); perforin and granzymes, leading to target apoptosis

stem: Technique Faner uses to size the FMR1 CGG-repeat expansion (Fragile X)
sourceRef: OST520 (061, 066) L - Molecular Techniques I and II - Faner.pdf, file p. 6; transcript 074 05:19-13:43

sourceRef: OST520 (061, 066) L - Molecular Techniques I and II - Faner.pdf, file p. 8-9; transcript 074 16:40-22:28
rationale:
Answer: Patient (test) DNA is labeled green and reference DNA is labeled red; an elevated green:red ratio indicates a patient gain, a reduced ratio indicates a patient loss [p9, 074 17:47-20:48].

sourceRef: OST520 (061, 066) L - Molecular Techniques I and II - Faner.pdf, file p. 12; transcript 074 32:12-35:12
rationale:
Answer: An LSI:CEP ratio greater than 2 is called amplification positive; a ratio below 2 is negative [p12, 074 33:01-35:12].

Discriminator: CEP counts chromosome copies as the control; LSI counts the gene locus itself. A higher raw LSI count alone (without a ratio above 2 relative to CEP) does not mean amplification [p12, 074 32:12-34:56].

stem: Why ARMS-PCR only produces a product when the mutant template is present
sourceRef: OST520 (061, 066) L - Molecular Techniques I and II - Faner.pdf, file p. 11; transcript 074 22:29-28:07
rationale:
Answer: The primer's 3' end is designed to match only the mutant sequence, and Taq polymerase cannot extend from a 3' mismatch, so a wild-type template blocks extension and no product forms [p11, 074 22:29-27:15].
